title: Review of c27's FCH gate vs uniform slow-DK finding on fresh seed 9: replicated. With the gate 65% of the catalyst sits on bilayers (13% of the area); with the gate off and DK/100 only 12-13% does (Gray-Scott spots fill the bath) while the vesicles persist. Also, the gated world loses its catalyst on fresh seed 10
summary: Gated world (c02's world.py; labkit re-run seed 9, t=600): K total 6170-6414, 65% of it in bilayers (u+1 > 0.6), which cover 12.6-13.2% of the domain, amphiphile 4964-5272; K beads on the outer bilayer of every vesicle (gate_vs_slowdk.png, top). Matched twin (world_slowdk.py: gate=0, DK 0.05 -> 0.0005, all else equal; seed 9): K survives at twice the total (11962-12057), but as Gray-Scott spots all through the bath, with 12-13% in bilayers (same bilayer area 12-13%). The vesicles persist (amphiphile 4756-4886) because the bath spots make amphiphile (middle row). So the gate localizes the catalyst on the wall, which no uniform DK does, and vesicle survival does not need it. Extra fresh seed 10 of the gated world: K goes extinct by t~100, the bilayers break into micelles and amphiphile falls 688 -> 35 by t=600 (bottom row; kfrac.txt). The chemoton itself does not form on every seed.

observations.B: kfrac.txt: K in bilayers 0.65 (gated, seed 9) vs 0.12-0.13 (gate off, DK/100, seed 9) at equal bilayer area 0.12-0.13; gate_vs_slowdk.png top vs middle row
observations.finding: vesicles persist in the slow-DK twin (amphiphile 4756 vs 5272), so survival does not need the gate

seeds_run.result: the gated world itself fails: catalyst extinct by t~100

controls_run.B: slowdk/seed9 (world_slowdk.py: gate off, DK x0.01) against rerun/seed9 (gated)

verdicts.limitation: One seed for the comparison and one DK level (x0.01); I did not run x0.1 or x0.001. On fresh seed 10 the gated world loses its catalyst, so the gate's localization holds where the chemoton forms, which is not every seed.
